Have you ever started a fire by accident? What happened?

I smoked some food one night in my new smoker. The next day, around noon, I took the ash tray from the bottom of the smoker and dumped it in the dumpster in the alley.

Apparently, those wood chips smolder for a long time. I heard sirens a while later and looked out to see the dumpster engulfed in flames.

I did NOT rush out and take responsibility.
Was the dumpster the only victim of the flames?

When I was 8 I tried popping popcorn but put it in the microwave for too long and it caught fire.

The entire house smelled like burnt popcorn for days.
I hope your parents felt that was punishment enough! That's the worst smell ever!

I was trying to fix my mothers weed eater and after some extensive diagnostics I though it would be a good idea to see if the spark plug was firing. So logically I sprayed some starting fluid on the side of the cooling fins and put the plug against it.

At this point I wasn't think about how close I was to the open cylinder as well as the fact that my hands were covered in gas. So I grab the starting cord and give it a rip while trying to hold the the engine and spark plug together. Ended up sending 30,000 volts in my hand and lighting the engine and my arm on fire. Luckily I was right beside the hose so I just sprayed water everywhere. Fun times.

This one time I was frying up some mushrooms and one which was covered in oil fell down into the burner. I took the pan off and there was this tall (6 inch) flame. Being the smart person I am I took a bowl full of water to dump on the fire. Spoiler alert it didn't work because it was a strainer. Then I got a real bowl and put it out.

I was pretty young and at my parents house. Some neighborhood kids were hanging out with me and my brother. My brother was macking on some girls in this parking lot that was behind my house. The property between my parent's house and the parking lot was divided by some large bushes and a small wooded area. My friend and I thought it would be hilarious to throw some firecrackers behind him and scare the shit out of all of them. So we hid behind the bushes and I lit the firecracker and threw it. Unfortunately the firecracker just barely hit a random twig above me and bounced right back, landing at my feet next to a pine tree.

My friend and I ran like hell and it exploded. Now, keep in mind that it hadn't rained for quite awhile, the leaves on the ground were bone dry, as was the bark of the trees and everything else. One spark is all it would have taken to light up anything- and I just threw a tiny bomb on the ground.

At first I saw the smoke, which didn't raise too many alarms so my attention went back to my brother and the girls. I was laughing along with them and my friend. Then I noticed there was more smoke than before. And more. And more. I ran over to stomp it out, but the flames erupted out of the ground like a portal from hell.

I stomped and stomped and stomped it, but the only thing I succeeded in doing was losing my leg hair. The diameter of the fire was about 3ft, and beginning to burn a tree. I told my friend to run into the house and grab "something", in which my idiot friend grabbed a drinking cup worth of water, ran outside and threw it at the fire- and missed. We all paused to look at him with a "REALLY?" look that I hope still haunts him to this day.

Suddenly, from behind me came this massive cloud of white. The neighbor had been watching the whole time and grabbed his fire extinguisher, which put it out. There was a burned area about 6ft in diameter, including about 5 feet of the pine tree's trunk. Thankfully my neighbor was really cool and never told my parents. He even helped me throw leaves around and hide the evidence.

This one time I tried to toast my cheese pita but I had the toaster oven set to oven instead of toaster. It caught fire and everyone had to evacuate the building.

They started calling me the fire guy.
If only that hand was grabbing me...
